1	# RedRoom Fitness — The Best HIIT Workout in the World
     2	
     3	## Brand
     4	RedRoom Fitness is the original high-intensity interval training experience, combining treadmill running and strength training in a signature red-lit studio environment. Founded for those who demand more from their workout, RedRoom delivers results through science-backed HIIT methodology across global studio locations and a digital on-demand platform. The tone is bold, dark, and unapologetically intense.
     5	
     6	Brand colors: `#FF0000` (RedRoom Red — primary), `#141414` (Charcoal Black — background), `#FFFFFF` (White — text/accent)
     7	
     8	## Hero Content
     9	Title: "TRY THE BEST WORKOUT IN THE WORLD™"
    10	Subtitle: "Buy an exclusive first-timer 3-pack and receive a FREE Fuel Shake or Grab + Go item after your third class."
    11	CTA: "BUY NOW" | "BOOK CLASSES"
    12	
    13	## Top Bar Promo
    14	Text: "The Best (Digital) Workout in the World"
    15	CTA: "Learn More" → links to Digital Platform page
    16	
    17	## Community Promo
    18	Heading: "Join the Hustle"
    19	Body: "Welcome to RedRoom. More than a workout — it's a movement. Our global community of athletes, first-timers, and everyone in between push limits together in the Red Room. Show up. Work hard. Earn your place."
    20	CTA: "Explore the Community"
    21	
    22	## Two Ways to Red Room
    23	Heading: "TWO WAYS TO RED ROOM"
    24	Option 1: **In-Studio** — "Get a (Red) Room. Step inside our signature red-lit studios for the full immersive experience. Heart-pounding music, elite instructors, and the energy of the pack."
    25	Option 2: **Digital** — "Go Digital. Stream world-class workouts from anywhere. Same intensity, your schedule."
    26	
    27	## The Workout — Method Overview
    28	Heading: "THE REDROOM WAY"
    29	Body: "Every class is a 50-minute full-body experience. You'll alternate between the treadmill and the floor, combining high-intensity cardio intervals with focused strength training. Our method is designed to maximize calorie burn, build lean muscle, and keep your metabolism elevated for hours after class. Hustle and heart set us apart."
    30	
    31	## Floor vs. Treadmill Toggle
    32	Heading: "Start on the Floor or the Treadmill"
    33	**Floor:** "Dumbbells, resistance bands, and bodyweight movements target specific muscle groups each day. Our instructors guide every rep to ensure proper form and maximum results."
    34	**Treadmill:** "From power walks to all-out sprints, the treadmill portion is designed to torch calories and build cardiovascular endurance. Every speed and incline is coach-led — all levels welcome."
    35	
    36	## Weekly Class Schedule
    37	
    38	| Day | Muscle Group Focus |
    39	|---|---|
    40	| Monday | Chest & Back |
    41	| Tuesday | Full Body (Lower Focus) |
    42	| Wednesday | Arms & Abs |
    43	| Thursday | Arms & Abs |
    44	| Friday | Full Body (Upper Focus) |
    45	| Saturday | Full Body |
    46	
    47	## Studio Experience
    48	Heading: "Meet Us in the Red Room."
    49	Body: "Red lights. Loud music. Zero distractions. Our studios are purpose-built for performance — every detail from the sound system to the lighting is engineered to push you harder. This isn't a gym. This is the Red Room."
    50	CTA: "THE BEST WORKOUT IN THE WORLD — Don't Wait. Book Now to Get the Red Room Experience."
    51	
    52	## Free Trial CTA
    53	Heading: "JOIN US FOR A FREE 30 DAY TRIAL"
    54	CTA: "Start Your Free Trial"
    55	
    56	## Instructor Roster
    57	
    58	Instructors are displayed as a filterable card grid. Each card shows: instructor name, home studio, and a "Book a Class" link.
    59	
    60	**Filter by location:** All Locations · New York · Los Angeles · London · Miami · San Francisco
    61	
    62	Sample instructors:
    63	- **Dani Reyes** — New York
    64	- **Marcus Cole** — Los Angeles
    65	- **Priya Nair** — London
    66	- **Jordan Voss** — Miami
    67	- **Tessa Kim** — San Francisco
    68	- **Andre Williams** — New York
    69	- **Sofia Marquez** — Los Angeles
    70	- **Liam Chen** — London
    71	
    72	CTA: "Get Started Today" | "Book a Class"
    73	
    74	## RIDE FAQ Content
    75	
    76	| Question | Answer |
    77	|---|---|
    78	| What is RIDE x LIFT? | RIDE x LIFT is RedRoom's signature cycling class that combines a high-energy spin session with strength training on the floor. It's 50 minutes of total-body work set to motivating playlists in our red-lit studio. |
    79	| What should I wear? | Wear moisture-wicking athletic clothing and supportive sneakers. Cycling shoes are available at the studio but not required. |
    80	| Do I need cycling shoes? | No. We provide complimentary cycling shoes at every RIDE x LIFT studio. You're welcome to bring your own SPD-compatible shoes if you prefer. |
    81	| How long is the class? | Each RIDE x LIFT class is 50 minutes — approximately 25 minutes on the bike and 25 minutes of strength work on the floor. |
    82	| Is RIDE x LIFT good for beginners? | Absolutely. Our instructors coach every level. You control your resistance and speed, so the workout scales to your fitness level. |
    83	| Where is RIDE x LIFT available? | RIDE x LIFT is currently available at our Chelsea, NYC studio with plans to expand to additional locations. |
    84	
    85	## Digital Platform Features
    86	
    87	Heading: "The Best (Digital) Workout in the World"
    88	
    89	- **World Class Workouts On Your Time** — Access RedRoom's signature HIIT classes filmed with top instructors. Treadmill, floor, and full-body formats available on demand.
    90	- **Workouts That Push You to Your Limits** — Strength, cardio, abs, stretching, and more. New classes added weekly across multiple categories and difficulty levels.
    91	- **Unlimited Access** — One membership, unlimited streaming. No caps on how many classes you take per week.
    92	- **30 Day Free Trial** — Try the full digital library free for 30 days. Cancel anytime.
    93	- **Anytime, Anywhere** — Stream on your phone, tablet, laptop, or TV. Your Red Room, wherever you are.
    94	
    95	CTA: "Join the Fit Fam Today" | "Start Your Free Trial"

     3	description: Create distinctive, production-grade static sites with React, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui — no mockups needed. Generates bold, memorable designs from plain text requirements with anti-AI-slop aesthetics, mobile-first responsive patterns, and single-file bundling. Use when building landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios, dashboards, or any static web UI. Supports both Vite (pure static) and Next.js (Vercel deploy) workflows.
     4	homepage: https://github.com/kesslerio/frontend-design-ultimate-clawhub-skill
     5	metadata:
     6	  openclaw:
     7	    emoji: "🎨"
     8	    requires:
     9	      bins: ["node", "npm"]
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	# Frontend Design Ultimate
    14	
    15	Create distinctive, production-grade static sites from text requirements alone. No mockups, no Figma — just describe what you want and get bold, memorable designs.
    16	
    17	**Stack**: React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui + Framer Motion  
    18	**Output**: Vite (static HTML) or Next.js (Vercel-ready)
    19	
    20	## Quick Start
    21	
    22	```
    23	"Build a SaaS landing page for an AI writing tool. Dark theme, 
    24	editorial typography, subtle grain texture. Pages: hero with 
    25	animated demo, features grid, pricing table, FAQ accordion, footer."
    26	```
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## Design Thinking (Do This First)
    31	
    32	Before writing any code, commit to a **BOLD aesthetic direction**:
    33	
    34	### 1. Understand Context
    35	
    36	- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
    37	- **Audience**: Developer tools? Consumer app? Enterprise? Creative agency?
    38	- **Constraints**: Performance requirements, accessibility needs, brand guidelines?
    39	
    40	### 2. Choose an Extreme Tone
    41	
    42	Pick ONE and commit fully — timid designs fail:
    43	
    44	| Tone                       | Characteristics                                           |
    45	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
    46	| **Brutally Minimal**       | Sparse, monochrome, massive typography, raw edges         |
    47	| **Maximalist Chaos**       | Layered, dense, overlapping elements, controlled disorder |
    48	| **Retro-Futuristic**       | Neon accents, geometric shapes, CRT aesthetics            |
    49	| **Organic/Natural**        | Soft curves, earth tones, hand-drawn elements             |
    50	| **Luxury/Refined**         | Subtle animations, premium typography, restrained palette |
    51	| **Editorial/Magazine**     | Strong grid, dramatic headlines, whitespace as feature    |
    52	| **Brutalist/Raw**          | Exposed structure, harsh contrasts, anti-design           |
    53	| **Art Deco/Geometric**     | Gold accents, symmetry, ornate patterns                   |
    54	| **Soft/Pastel**            | Rounded corners, gentle gradients, friendly               |
    55	| **Industrial/Utilitarian** | Functional, monospace, data-dense                         |
    56	
    57	### 3. Define the Unforgettable Element
    58	
    59	What's the ONE thing someone will remember? A hero animation? Typography treatment? Color combination? Unusual layout?
    60	
    61	---
    62	
    63	## Aesthetics Guidelines
    64	
    65	### Typography — NEVER Generic
    66	
    67	**BANNED**: Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts, Open Sans
    68	
    69	**DO**: Distinctive, characterful choices that elevate the design.
    70	
    71	| Use Case          | Approach                                                     |
    72	| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
    73	| Display/Headlines | Bold personality — Clash, Cabinet Grotesk, Satoshi, Space Grotesk (sparingly), Playfair Display |
    74	| Body Text         | Refined readability — Instrument Sans, General Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans |
    75	| Monospace/Code    | DM Mono, JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono                       |
    76	| Pairing Strategy  | Contrast weights (thin display + bold body), contrast styles (serif + geometric sans) |
    77	
    78	**Size Progression**: Use 3x+ jumps, not timid 1.5x increments.
    79	
    80	### Color & Theme
    81	
    82	**BANNED**: Purple gradients on white, evenly-distributed 5-color palettes
    83	
    84	**DO**:
    85	
    86	- **Dominant + Sharp Accent**: 70-20-10 rule (primary-secondary-accent)
    87	- **CSS Variables**: `--primary`, `--accent`, `--surface`, `--text`
    88	- **Commit to dark OR light**: Don't hedge with gray middle-grounds
    89	- **High contrast CTAs**: Buttons should pop dramatically
    90	
    91	```css
    92	:root {
    93	  --bg-primary: #0a0a0a;
    94	  --bg-secondary: #141414;
    95	  --text-primary: #fafafa;
    96	  --text-secondary: #a1a1a1;
    97	  --accent: #ff6b35;
    98	  --accent-hover: #ff8555;
    99	}
   100	```
   101	
   102	### Motion & Animation
   103	
   104	**Priority**: One orchestrated page load > scattered micro-interactions
   105	
   106	**High-Impact Moments**:
   107	
   108	- Staggered hero reveals (`animation-delay`)
   109	- Scroll-triggered section entrances
   110	- Hover states that surprise (scale, color shift, shadow depth)
   111	- Smooth page transitions
   112	
   113	**Implementation**:
   114	
   115	- CSS-only for simple animations
   116	- Framer Motion for React (pre-installed via init scripts)
   117	- Keep durations 200-400ms (snappy, not sluggish)
   118	
   119	### Spatial Composition
   120	
   121	**BANNED**: Centered, symmetrical, predictable layouts
   122	
   123	**DO**:
   124	
   125	- Asymmetry with purpose
   126	- Overlapping elements
   127	- Diagonal flow / grid-breaking
   128	- Generous negative space OR controlled density (pick one)
   129	- Off-grid hero sections
   130	
   131	### Backgrounds & Atmosphere
   132	
   133	**BANNED**: Solid white/gray backgrounds
   134	
   135	**DO**:
   136	
   137	- Gradient meshes (subtle, not garish)
   138	- Noise/grain textures (SVG filter or CSS)
   139	- Geometric patterns (dots, lines, shapes)
   140	- Layered transparencies
   141	- Dramatic shadows for depth
   142	- Blur effects for glassmorphism
   143	
   144	```css
   145	/* Subtle grain overlay */
   146	.grain::before {
   147	  content: '';
   148	  position: fixed;
   149	  inset: 0;
   150	  background: url("data:image/svg+xml,...") repeat;
   151	  opacity: 0.03;
   152	  pointer-events: none;
   153	}
   154	```
   155	
   156	---
   157	
   158	## Mobile-First Patterns
   159	
   160	See **[references/mobile-patterns.md](references/mobile-patterns.md)** for detailed CSS.
   161	
   162	### Critical Rules
   163	
   164	| Pattern                 | Desktop           | Mobile Fix                                   |
   165	| ----------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
   166	| Hero with hidden visual | 2-column grid     | Switch to `display: flex` (not grid)         |
   167	| Large selection lists   | Horizontal scroll | Accordion with category headers              |
   168	| Multi-column forms      | Side-by-side      | Stack vertically                             |
   169	| Status/alert cards      | Inline            | `align-items: center` + `text-align: center` |
   170	| Feature grids           | 3-4 columns       | Single column                                |
   171	
   172	### Breakpoints
   173	
   174	```css
   175	/* Tablet - stack sidebars */
   176	@media (max-width: 1200px) { }
   177	
   178	/* Mobile - full single column */
   179	@media (max-width: 768px) { }
   180	
   181	/* Small mobile - compact spacing */
   182	@media (max-width: 480px) { }
   183	```
   184	
   185	### Font Scaling
   186	
   187	```css
   188	@media (max-width: 768px) {
   189	  .hero-title { font-size: 32px; }      /* from ~48px */
   190	  .section-title { font-size: 24px; }   /* from ~32px */
   191	  .section-subtitle { font-size: 14px; } /* from ~16px */
   192	}
   193	```
   194	
   195	---
   196	
   197	## Build Workflow
   198	
   199	### Option A: Vite (Pure Static) — Recommended (Offline)
   200	
   201	A pre-built Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui template with all dependencies is available at `/app/templates/vite-react`. Use it directly without network access:
   202	
   203	```bash
   204	# 1. Copy the pre-installed template
   205	cp -r /app/templates/vite-react my-site
   206	cd my-site
   207	
   208	# 2. Develop — edit src/App.tsx, add components in src/components/
   209	# All shadcn/ui components (button, badge, card, accordion, dialog,
   210	# navigation-menu, tabs, sheet, separator, avatar, alert) are pre-installed.
   211	# Framer Motion, Lucide icons, and Tailwind CSS are ready to use.
   212	
   213	# 3. Build static files
   214	npm run build
   215	# Output: dist/
   216	
   217	# 4. Bundle to single HTML (optional)
   218	bash /app/skills/scripts/bundle-artifact.sh
   219	# Output: bundle.html
   220	```
   221	
   222	### Option B: Init from Scratch (Requires Internet)
   223	
   224	If internet access is available, you can scaffold from scratch:
   225

#!/bin/bash
# Bundle a Vite React project into a single HTML file
# Usage: bash scripts/bundle-artifact.sh
# Run from project root (where package.json is)

set -e

echo "📦 Bundling to single HTML file..."

# Check if we're in a project directory
if [ ! -f "package.json" ]; then
  echo "❌ Error: No package.json found. Run this from your project root."
  exit 1
fi

# Check if index.html exists
if [ ! -f "index.html" ]; then
  echo "❌ Error: No index.html found in project root."
  exit 1
fi

# Install bundling dependencies if needed
if ! npm ls parcel > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "📦 Installing bundling dependencies..."
  npm install -D parcel @parcel/config-default parcel-resolver-tspaths html-inline
fi

# Create .parcelrc if it doesn't exist
if [ ! -f ".parcelrc" ]; then
  echo "⚙️ Creating Parcel config..."
  cat > .parcelrc << 'EOF'
{
  "extends": "@parcel/config-default",
  "resolvers": ["parcel-resolver-tspaths", "..."]
}
EOF
fi

# Build with Parcel
echo "🔨 Building with Parcel..."
npx parcel build index.html --no-source-maps --dist-dir dist-parcel

# Inline all assets
echo "📄 Inlining assets into single HTML..."
npx html-inline -i dist-parcel/index.html -o bundle.html -b dist-parcel

# Clean up
rm -rf dist-parcel .parcel-cache

# Get file size
SIZE=$(ls -lh bundle.html | awk '{print $5}')

echo ""
echo "✅ Bundle created: bundle.html ($SIZE)"
echo ""
echo "You can now share this file or use it as a Claude artifact."
echo ""
